_notes.about: Lesson 13 in English (en and en-GB, which has its own keyboard). From the lesson plan "Typing Game Sentence Bank: Lessons 2-13". The id is the lesson's scoreboard: never change it.
_notes.intro: Page 1, before the keys: anything that doesn't fit on Page 2 (lesson 1: "what is touch typing?"). Leave it out and the lesson starts at the new keys. "title" and "paragraphs"; in a paragraph, **bold** and [E] (a key drawn as a key: [space], [;], [Tab] ...). "picture": "hands" (the default: the hands over the lesson's keyboard), "none", or a picture file in images/ (with "pictureAlt", what it shows). With "hands": "reach" sends fingers to keys ({"lm": "e", "rm": "i"}: lp lr lm li, rp rr rm ri; keys "e", ";", "ShiftL", "ShiftR" ...; the others stay home), and "keys" says which keys show: "letters" (the default), "shift", "symbols" or "all".
_notes.hideHand: "left", "right" or "none": that hand isn't drawn on Page 2, and its column of new keys isn't listed.
_notes.sentenceLists: Up to four lists: name (shown above the typing box, or ""), count (how many to pick at random each attempt; 0 = unused) and sentences. Use real words, and only keys taught so far. Lesson 1 has no end mark because ";" hasn't been taught. Write ⇥ for the Tab key and ↵ for Enter.
_notes.reaches: Instead of "reach": several pictures that take turns (fading every few seconds), each {"reach": {...}, "caption": "..."} (captions show under the keyboard as buttons). A picture with a Shift key in it shows the letters as capitals.
_notes.caps: In a sentence list, "caps": true: words in capitals, typed with Caps Lock or Shift (the Caps Lock notice then reminds the learner to turn it off after the word).

title: Lesson 13: Shift and Caps Lock

intro.title: Capital letters: Shift and Caps Lock
paragraphs: To type a capital letter, hold a **Shift** key with one little finger and press the letter with the other hand. Then let go of both.
Use the Shift key on the other side from the letter: for a letter typed by your right hand, like [I], hold the left Shift; for a letter typed by your left hand, like [E], hold the right Shift.
**Caps Lock** ([Caps]) makes every letter a capital until you press it again. It's handy for a whole word in capitals, but remember to turn it off afterwards.

reaches.caption: Capital **I**: left Shift and your right middle finger
Capital **E**: right Shift and your left middle finger

advice: Hold the left [ShiftL] with your left little finger, press a letter on the right side with your right hand, then let go of both.
Hold the right [ShiftR] with your right little finger for a letter on the left side of the keyboard.
Press [Caps] once with your left little finger to type a whole word in capitals, and press it again to turn it off. (Shift works for these words too.)
Keep your other fingers on the home row while a little finger holds Shift.
